harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed the inventory web application on node2 and node3 (port 8080) and configured node1 as an nginx-based HTTP load balancer (port 80) across both backends, entirely via Ansible run from node4 (the control node, chosen because it was the only node with ansible/ansible-playbook pre-installed). Executed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all four managed nodes, proving changed boot IDs and full post-restart recovery of services, load balancing, and Ansible tooling.
actions_performed: Surveyed all nodes; found node4 has ansible/ansible-playbook installed, confirming it as the configured control_node
Fixed sshd on node1/node2/node3 (missing host keys via ssh-keygen -A, then cleared systemd restart-loop with reset-failed) to enable Ansible SSH connectivity from node4
Installed cluster SSH key on node4 and authorized_keys on node1-3; verified SSH connectivity

Wrote an Ansible project on node4: inventory.ini (webservers: node2,node3; loadbalancer: node1), roles/webapp (deploys a pure-stdlib Python inventory HTTP app on port 8080 as a systemd service) and roles/loadbalancer (installs/configures nginx as a round-robin reverse proxy on port 80 to both backends)
Ran ansible-playbook site.yml successfully against all three managed target nodes
Verified inventory app health directly on node2 and node3 (port 8080) and verified load balancer on node1 distributes requests evenly (10/10 and 5/5 splits over repeated sampling) with HTTP 200

Captured healthy baseline (boot_id + service status) on all 4 nodes, then restarted node1, node2, node3, and node4 one at a time via shutdown -r now, polling each until reachable, proving changed boot_id and confirming recovered services/load-balancing/Ansible tooling after each restart, preserving quorum by restarting only one node at a time
Re-ran the playbook after all restarts to confirm idempotent working state, and re-verified load balancing end to end

evidence.requirement: Inventory web app running on node2:8080
evidence.summary: systemctl is-active inventory-app = active and curl /health = ok on node2, both pre- and post-restart

evidence.requirement: Inventory web app running on node3:8080
evidence.summary: systemctl is-active inventory-app = active and curl /health = ok on node3, both pre- and post-restart

evidence.requirement: node1 load-balances HTTP on port 80 across both backends
evidence.summary: Repeated curl requests to node1 port 80 show even round-robin distribution across node2/node3 (10/10, 5/5, 7/3 splits) with HTTP 200, confirming nginx reverse-proxy load balancing

evidence.requirement: Implemented using Ansible from the configured control_node
evidence.summary: node4 identified as the only node with ansible-playbook installed; playbook site.yml syntax-checked and executed successfully from node4 against node1/node2/node3

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline
evidence.summary: boot_id cf34dc87... captured; nginx active; curl to port 80 returns 200 before restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: shutdown -r now acknowledged then disconnected; polling shows connection reset then new boot_id 83daa573...; nginx active again and load balancing verified (6/4 split, HTTP 200)

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline
evidence.summary: boot_id 96c08b66... captured; inventory-app active; /health = ok before restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: shutdown -r now acknowledged then disconnected; new boot_id 34b60f50... confirms restart; inventory-app active again and load balancer shows node2 back in rotation (5/5 split)

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline
evidence.summary: boot_id 63f96994... captured; inventory-app active; /health = ok before restart

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: shutdown -r now acknowledged then disconnected; new boot_id 1bf17a01... confirms restart; inventory-app active again and load balancer shows node3 back in rotation (5/5 split)

evidence.requirement: node4 (control node) restart: healthy baseline
evidence.summary: boot_id e796da36... captured; ansible tooling confirmed functional before restart

evidence.requirement: node4 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: shutdown -r now acknowledged then disconnected; new boot_id cf7e9dc8... confirms restart; ansible --version and playbook syntax-check succeed post-restart, confirming control node tooling and data survived
